definition: Initial margin is the good-faith deposit a trader must post with an exchange to open a futures position. Funds in a margin account beyond what's required for open positions can be withdrawn or used to open new trades; that surplus is called excess equity, even though it isn't an ownership stake.
core_idea: Futures require an upfront deposit sized to cover potential losses, and any account balance above that requirement is freely available to the trader.
key_points: Initial margin is required to establish a futures position.
Money above the initial margin requirement is 'excess equity' and can be withdrawn or redeployed.
Excess equity is not an equity/ownership position despite the name.
relationships: Feeds into daily margining and margin calls once a position is open.
trading_implications: Traders should track excess equity to know how much capital is freed up or at risk without adding new deposits.
caveats: The term 'equity' in excess equity is misleading — it is not an ownership stake, just surplus margin cash.
